thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: urgent: sustained p95 latency regression on model-serving-prod (eu-west) detected. alert window 10m, p95=2.4s (baseline 260ms). Auto-collect: traces, node metrics, kube events.

lena: oncall here. looking at traces now. @arjun can you join for kernel/infra context?

arjun: joining. pulling node list. which AZs impacted?

observability-bot: affected AZs: eu-west-2a and eu-west-2c. Top endpoints: /v2/embeddings (55%), /v2/generate (40%). Error rate steady. Slow traces sample: https://observability.internal/traces?id=0xdea456 (shared).

theo: preliminary numbers: p50 140ms -> 330ms; p95 260ms -> 2400ms. GPU times unchanged. Host-side syscall stalls visible (epoll_wait and epoll_pwait). Network retransmits slightly higher but not catastrophic.

arjun: kernel versions: eu-west-2a nodes on 6.1.7-custom; 2c nodes on 5.15. Nodes on 6.1 show degradation. We pushed a security boot patch this morning that included a net subsystem tweak.

lena: hypothesis list: H1: 6.1 net subsystem NAPI changes causing processing stalls; H2: dispatcher's ephemeral sockets + accept churn causing epoll ptr race; H3: workload change (sudden spike of small requests).

ops-bot: flagging incident P1 and paging infra owners.

arjun: pulled dmesg from node gpu-eu2-04: ```
Mar 22 09:11:02 gpu-eu2-04 kernel: [98765.432100] possible deadlock detected in epoll wait loop
Mar 22 09:11:02 model-server[7211]: WARN dispatcher: accept loop slow; accept latency 480ms
Mar 22 09:11:03 model-server[7211]: INFO conn: ephemeral connections 1400/min
```

theo: trace span breakdown for one 2.3s request (trace 0xdea456):
- request enqueue to dispatcher: 610ms
- userland poll/epoll wait: 900ms
- model forward (GPU): 150ms
- response serialization: 40ms

lena: that's strongly pointing to epoll/userland wait. I'm going to cordon and drain one 6.1 node to see effect. Also let's try a quick sysctl ramp: `sysctl -w net.core.somaxconn=10240` and `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_max_syn_backlog=4096` on a single node as experiment.

arjun: applied somaxconn/tcp_max_syn_backlog on gpu-eu2-04. also toggled `net.core.netdev_max_backlog=4000` for one node. results: minor improvement but not full.

theo: after draining gpu-eu2-04, cluster p95 dropped to ~360ms within 90s. draining another 6.1 node gpu-eu2-06 shows same. nodes on 5.15 unaffected.

observability-bot: p95 timeline: 09:10 alert -> 2.4s peak; 09:14 drain 04 -> 420ms; 09:18 drain 06 -> 330ms; 09:30 stabilized ~300ms.

lena: customer impact: 78 API keys saw >1s responses; 3 customers opened support tickets. No SLA outages but user experience impacted. I'll draft proactive comms for top impacted customers.

arjun: kernel diff notes between 5.15 and 6.1 patchset: ```
- NAPI: fixed batching heuristics and changed interrupt/softirq wakeup thresholds
- net: new batching for epoll to reduce wakeups under high fd counts
- skb: different rx queue processing ordering
```

theo: local repro: created high-churn ephemeral TCP scenario (connect/send/close ~1000/s) against dispatcher; epoll_wait latency increases significantly on 6.1. Confirmed reproduction of dispatcher enqueue wait.

lena: current prioritization: short-term = cordon 6.1 nodes, shift traffic to 5.15 pool; short-mid = runtime patch to use long-lived keepalive connections and connection pooling; mid-long = block kernel rollout to latency fleets until perf sign-off and work upstream if needed.

arjun: infra note: the 6.1 rollout was part of auto-update channel started at 02:00. We'll pause and roll back 6.1 on the remaining latency-sensitive hosts. Scheduling rollback now.

theo: I've uploaded trace and perf bundles: s3://redwood-incidents/1823459999/bundles/ (includes strace, perf, full spans). Perf counters snapshot from gpu-eu2-06 before drain: ```
perf stat -e context-switches,cs,cycles,cache-misses -I 1000
1000, 9000, 13,210,000, 47,800
2000, 16000, 11,950,000, 58,120
```

lena: handoff: I'm putting @arjun in the lead for rollback tracking and infra coordination. @theo please continue trace aggregation and repro notes. I'll handle customer comms and incident doc.

arjun: rollback in progress for remaining 6.1 hosts in eu-west pool. ETA 50m. smoke tests queued.

observability-bot: post-rollback metrics: p95 back to baseline ~320ms in 12m after rollback. No errors introduced.

theo: adding to hypothesis tracker: H1 high confidence: NAPI/epoll batching changes in 6.1 introduced increased epoll_wait tail latency under ephemeral connection churn used by our dispatcher. H2 low. runtime changes will mitigate impact.

lena: timeline snippet for incident doc: ```
- 09:10:22 alert triggered for p95 spike
- 09:11:05 initial paging; lena ack
- 09:12:30 traces sampled and node correlation identified
- 09:14:10 cordon/gpu-eu2-04; experiment sysctl knobs applied
- 09:16:45 p95 decreased, but still elevated
- 09:18:30 cordon/gpu-eu2-06; p95 near baseline
- 09:35:00 rollback of 6.1 started for remaining nodes
- 10:20:00 service stabilized; rollback complete
```

arjun: uploading kernel build/packaging differences and the rollout plan to the infra board. link: https://infra.internal/rollouts/1823459999 (private)

theo: reproductions and perf graphs attached to the incident doc. linking upstream kernel bug: https://kernel-archive.org/6.1-epoll-batching-issue-2026 (tracking).

lena: customer comm drafted: "We observed increased latency for certain model-serving calls during a maintenance window this morning caused by a host kernel update. We rolled back the update for latency-sensitive hosts and performance has been restored. We're implementing runtime connection pooling and gating hosts for future kernel upgrades. A full RCA will follow."

arjun: follow-ups assigned: (1) infra: implement rollout gating for fleets with latency SLOs (infra) (2) eng-runtime: implement keepalive/connection-pool and dispatcher backpressure (theo + eng-runtime) (3) infra: improve preflight perf tests for kernel updates (arjun) (4) postmortem doc with perf counters and kernel diffs (lena).

ops-bot: Incident 1823459999 status updated to mitigated. Postmortem scheduled 2026-03-08 10:00 UTC.

lena: final note: primary probable root cause = kernel network/NAPI/epoll batching change in 6.1 interacting poorly with our ephemeral connection pattern. Mitigations: rollback, runtime pooling, infra gating. Great work triaging and rapid mitigation team. :clap:
